answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each agent identity must accumulate solved task records on a shared append-only ledger; weights depend on task diversity, so repeating trivial work yields diminishing credit. A new identity starts at zero and must redo the slow accumulation from scratch. The karst of task categories is deliberately deep, forcing months of varied output. A verification lantern periodically audits a random sample, and forged records are struck, resetting the identity to basalt—bare stone, no history. Attacker cost: sustained real labor per clone, not money.
